newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi satisfied with Prince Sultan's U.S. visit.
newsitem.headline: Saudi satisfied with Prince Sultan's U.S. visit.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said it was satisfied with the results of last week's visit to the United States by Defence Minister Prince Sultan which it said consolidated friendship between the two countries.

"The kingdom is satisfied with the results of the visit of Prince Sultan to the United States," said a statement issued after a weekly Saudi cabinet meeting on Monday night. It was carried by the official Saudi Press Agency.

The cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Abdullah, also praised President Bill Clinton and senior U.S. officials for expressing "keeness to have mutual, and equal relations between the kingdom and the United States".
It said such relations "serve the interests of both countries and consolidate existing friendship based on mutual respect and trust".

Washington has said it received renewed pledges during Prince Sultan's visit of cooperation in investigating a bombing that killed 19 U.S servicemen in eastern Saudi Arabia -- a sour point in bilateral ties.
Washington had complained that Saudi Arabia was not sharing enough information on the June 1996 bombing which devastated a U.S. military housing complex in Dhahran.
Prince Sultan was on Sunday quoted as saying Saudi Arabia and the United States had agreed to set up a hotline between their defence ministers to boost cooperation.
